models.name: Gemini Decision 1
models.note: Scoring model behind the Gemini Decisions API: returns calibrated picks for yes/no, multiple-choice, and rubric questions (up to 1,000 per request) instead of generating text. 150-250 ms latency. Free tier in AI Studio.

models.name: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Preview
models.note: Post-trained version of ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base: 280B MoE, 14B active. API on Baidu Qianfan; Baidu says weights will follow under Apache 2.0. Baidu calls it an intermediate checkpoint.

models.name: Qwen4-Max Preview
models.note: First Qwen4 model. 15-day preview to Nov 25 for interactive coding and agent use; no benchmarks, parameter count, or weights published. Text, image, and video in; thinking on by default.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.2
models.note: Anthropic's top generally available model, 20% cheaper than 5.1 and under GPT-6 Astra. Leads Anthropic's own coding and agent benchmarks. Same model as Mythos 5.2, which has looser cyber and bio safeguards and is restricted to vetted partners.

models.name: Muse Ember
models.note: Meta's small agent-execution model. Same sticker price as Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna, but uses fewer tokens per task on Artificial Analysis's index.

models.name: LongCat-2.5
models.note: 1.6T-parameter (~48B active) multimodal MoE built for agentic and visual coding, optimized for Chinese accelerators. Big gains over LongCat-2.0, but trails top US models on Terminal Bench 4.0.

models.name: Arete-27B
models.note: Fine-tune of Alibaba's Qwen3.8-27B to stop giving Chinese state positions. Nous says propaganda-tagged answers fell from 22% to 0.9% on its own eval with little capability change; not independently verified.

models.name: Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash
models.note: Video generation model, now generally available. Clips up to 15 seconds with multi-turn edits; 30% cheaper than before. In Gemini API, Google Cloud, Flow, Vids, Ads, and the Gemini app (Ultra).

models.name: Inkling 2 Small
models.note: 594B MoE, 17B active, text and image input. Closed on Tinker for now; Apache 2.0 weights promised the week of Nov 9 after outside safety testing. AA Intelligence Index 31.

models.name: GPT-6 Cyber
models.note: Security model for vulnerability discovery and exploit validation. Approved Daybreak Red customers only, via API and Codex. Rated Critical for cyber risk by OpenAI. Pricing not disclosed.

models.name: ERNIE 5.5 Flash Base
models.note: 280B MoE, 14B active, 33.5T training tokens. Base model only, no chat tuning; tuned version promised. Custom Baidu license.

models.name: SWE-2 Flash
models.note: Coding model for Devin, built on Thinking Machines' open Inkling-Small. 276B MoE, 12B active. Cognition says 3x faster and 1/5 the cost of SWE-2 but weaker on Terminal-Bench and DeepSWE. Free in Devin through Nov 30.

models.name: Hy4
models.note: Full release of Tencent's 770B MoE (preview was Apache 2.0 open weights). Adds vision and computer use. Weights and system card promised later. 50% launch discount on OpenRouter.

models.name: Gemini 4 Carbon
models.note: Google's top model. Open to paid API, business, and AI Ultra users since Nov 10 (cyber-specialized version still restricted to vetted defenders). 60 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 4th behind Claude Fable 5.2. Uses many more output tokens than most models, so cost per task is higher than the price suggests.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Terra
models.note: Mid-tier model tuned for computer use, visual reasoning, and everyday work. About half the price of GPT-6.1 Sol.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
models.note: 2.8T-parameter MoE (104B active), 4-bit MXFP4 weights (1.56 TB). Weights posted Nov 4 under a custom license: API resellers with over $20M in revenue need a separate deal. Moonshot reports 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 (Opus 5.5: 66.4%).

models.name: Gemini 4 Argon
models.note: Google's generally available Gemini 4. Takes text, image, video, audio, and PDF. Has computer use, search grounding, and low/medium/high thinking. Not on the free API tier.

models.name: Muse Wonder
models.note: Meta's frontier API model. Takes text, image, video, and audio. The bigger Muse Wonder Full (Intelligence Index 56) is only available in Muse Code ($50/mo).

models.name: Muse Spark Open
models.note: MoE with 816B total / 42B active parameters. Top US open-weight model on the Intelligence Index (39). License: commercial use only for companies under $20M revenue.

models.name: Claude Haiku 5.5
models.note: Cheapest Claude model. First Haiku with an adjustable effort setting.

models.name: Mistral Large 4
models.note: MoE with 1T total / ~52B active parameters, multimodal. Weights released Oct 29 under a modified MIT license (free in-house; hosting it as a service needs a commercial license). Quantized version needs about 4 B200/B300 GPUs.

models.name: GPT-6.1 Sol
models.note: OpenAI's main workhorse model for coding and professional work.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5.5
models.note: About 30% faster than Sonnet 5 and up to 30% cheaper on most work. The balanced middle tier.

models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.note: Anthropic's flagship generally available model. Close to Mythos-tier results on most work at much lower cost.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.note: OpenAI's cheapest tier, for high-volume simple tasks.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.note: xAI's current flagship. Output priced below Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash
models.note: Smallest model in DeepSeek's V4 family, with native image understanding.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.note: OpenAI's most capable model. Expensive, so save it for the hardest work.

models.name: DeepSeek V4
models.note: 1.6T-parameter MoE. China's flagship open-weight model family this year.
